LOOP ITERATION 15. Round 9: ONE blocking finding, down from 11 (round 8) and 14 (round 7). The split
is what did that — same plan, same author, one concern removed.

THE FINDING IS MY RECURRING BLIND SPOT, FOR THE FOURTH TIME: I added the observability AC last
iteration and never propagated the MECHANISM into Approach or Scope. The criterion said what must be
true and nothing said how. Same shape as J9's Scope file list (twice) and J8's Approach omissions
(once). The pattern is specific and worth naming precisely: I add or revise an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION
and leave the sections that tell an implementer WHAT TO DO untouched.

FIXED, and investigating it turned up the reason the gap existed at all: transport.py has ZERO
logging references — no 'import logging', no logger, nothing. That is exactly WHY a failure in one of
the seven swallowed members surfaces nothing today; there is no channel for it to surface through.
The plan now specifies:
 * add the module-level convention the sibling adapters already use — 'import logging' +
   'logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)', as adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:13,25 does;
 * each newly-implemented member logs at WARNING naming the MEMBER and the REMOTE ID before the error
   propagates (J10 has already translated it to BackendHTTPError by that point);
 * use the LOGGER, not alert_store — alert_store.append(record, repo_root) needs a repo_root the
   transport does not have and should not acquire, since a vendor adapter is not a store client.
   Sibling adapters use logger.warning for exactly this class of event (acli_cli_ops.py:415,
   acli_subprocess.py:135,140, jira_family/sanitizers.py:85), so this follows the established
   convention instead of inventing a second one.

Scope now names transport.py as gaining the logger, so the file list matches the Approach. Round 10
running.
